newsitem.title: USA: Power group says outage could have been avoided.
newsitem.headline: Power group says outage could have been avoided.

text.p: The Western Systems Coordinating Council Wednesday said an August 10 blackout that affected millions of customers in the Western United States could have been prevented if contingency plans had been adopted.

In a preliminary report issued late Wednesday, the group said the outage could have been less severe if plans had been adopted to minimize the effects of an outage of the Keeler Allston 500,000-volt line in the Pacific Northwest. In addition, the task force determined the loss of the McNary generating units and inadequate tree-trimming practices, operating studies and instructions to dispatchers played a significant role in the outage.
The task force made a total of 30 conclusions, including the following:
-- Prior to the disturbance, the interconnected transmission system was "unknowingly" being operated in a manner that was not in compliance with the Council's reliability criteria.

-- The loss of the 13 McNary hydroelectric generating units in the northwest was a major factor leading to the outage of the transmission lines between the Pacific Northwest and California, and the subsequent islanding of the Council's interconnected system.
The group said the amount of power on the Pacific Intertie has been reduced pending a review by the Council and all member have been asked to review their tree trimming programs.
